name: ANTLR Software Rights Notice with license fallback
text:
ANTLR 2 License

We reserve no legal rights to the ANTLR--it is fully in the public domain. An individual or company may do whatever they wish with source code distributed with ANTLR or the code generated by ANTLR, including the incorporation of ANTLR, or its output, into commerical software.

We encourage users to develop software with ANTLR. However, we do ask that credit is given to us for developing ANTLR. By "credit", we mean that if you use ANTLR or incorporate any source code into one of your programs (commercial product, research project, or otherwise) that you acknowledge this fact somewhere in the documentation, research report, etc... If you like ANTLR and have developed a nice tool with the output, please mention that you developed it using ANTLR. In addition, we ask that the headers remain intact in our source code. As long as these guidelines are kept, we expect to continue enhancing this system and expect to make other tools available as they are completed.

In countries where the Public Domain status of the work may not be valid, the author grants a copyright licence to the general public to deal in the work without restriction and permission to sublicence derivates under the terms of any (OSI approved) Open Source licence.

comments: ANTLR used a public domain notice through version 2.7 and then switched to a BSD license for version 3.0 and later. Their original notice did not include the third paragraph with the fallback license listed here; see ANTLR-PD for the version without this third paragraph.

evidence.locator: text: first paragraph ('fully in the public domain' and permission to do whatever the user wishes) and final paragraph ('deal in the work without restriction' plus permission to sublicense derivatives under any OSI-approved Open Source license); neither regime imposes a same-license or reciprocal-source condition

metadata: name='ANTLR Software Rights Notice with license fallback'; text: first paragraph ('fully in the public domain') and final paragraph (a copyright license applies where public-domain status may not be valid); public-domain-equivalent records the dedication purpose but the single family value cannot represent the alternative permissive copyright regime losslessly

text: second paragraph asks for acknowledgment in documentation or a research report and asks that source headers remain intact, but calls these requests 'ask' and 'guidelines' rather than conditions of the unrestricted grant; the vocabulary cannot distinguish requested attribution/header preservation from binding notice duties, represented by unknown

text: second paragraph requests credit and intact source headers without stating them as grant conditions; final paragraph permits sublicensing derivatives only under an OSI-approved Open Source license; the vocabulary has no value for a nonbinding request or this alternative-license selection condition, represented by unknown; no source-disclosure, corresponding-source, same-license, or license-text duty is stated
text: complete license review (the public-domain statement and fallback copyright license contain no express patent grant, patent-claim restriction, or patent-assertion termination)

text: first paragraph permits individuals and companies to do whatever they wish with ANTLR source and generated code, expressly including incorporation into commercial software; final paragraph grants the public a copyright license to deal in the work without restriction and expressly permits sublicensing derivatives under an OSI-approved Open Source license; these statements support commercial use, distribution, modification, private use, and sublicensing, but not an express patent grant

text: final paragraph limits permission to sublicense derivatives to terms of an OSI-approved Open Source license, a condition not represented by the restriction vocabulary and therefore recorded as unknown; complete text contains no warranty disclaimer, liability limitation, trademark restriction, or patent-claim restriction

metadata: id=ANTLR-PD-fallback, name='ANTLR Software Rights Notice with license fallback', deprecated=false, osi=false, fsf=false; comments distinguish this identifier from ANTLR-PD by the third fallback paragraph; text: first and final paragraphs create jurisdiction-dependent public-domain and copyright-license regimes, while the final paragraph also constrains derivative sublicensing to any OSI-approved Open Source license and the second paragraph makes attribution/header requests whose binding status the vocabulary cannot encode; these alternatives and predicates cannot be communicated losslessly by the single-valued guide model, so the profile is not safe for general recommendation
